narrative:
Direct transport costs are about 85% of revenue. Subcontracted transport (affrètement, FTL carriers, air and sea lines) is the largest line at about 51% of revenue, followed by direct labour (22%), own-fleet fuel (5.5%) and fleet and hub costs (7%).

The Q1 diesel spike hit two lines at once: own-fleet fuel and the fuel embedded in carrier rates, which carriers re-price after one month — faster than Heppner's own surcharge. Net revenue (revenue minus subcontracting) holds at about 49% of revenue.

The freight-flow optimisation model saved 2.5% of subcontracted road km in Q3 (€0.58M); last-mile subcontracting is the leak, 14% above plan in Rouen and Marseille-Vitrolles.

signals.title: Q1 diesel spike: surcharge recovered two months late
signals.source: SDP agency margin monitor — CNR diesel index vs fuel surcharge (synthetic data)
signals.excerpt: The CNR diesel index rose about 20% between January and March 2026 (€1.52 → €1.82 per litre). The fuel surcharge followed with a two-month lag, so about €0.7M of agency contribution margin was lost in Q1.

signals.title: Freight-flow optimisation saves 2.5% of subcontracted km
signals.source: Freight-flow ML (TMS → Kafka → Snowpipe Streaming) — groupings accepted by freight agents
signals.excerpt: Every 10 minutes the model proposes shipment groupings. Accepted groupings saved about 2.5% of subcontracted km in Q3 2026 (356k km, about €0.58M), which now flows into the subcontracting plan.
